shapes_keyed_by: port index as a string; the output port of this export is unnamed, so there is no name to key by
named_port_keys_note: the port key of each entry of output_names, in order; output_names is compacted, so a name alone cannot say which port it belongs to
fetch_note: MEASURED on the installed runtime by this tool; see fetch_api for the per-call results. The two sides want DIFFERENT key types and neither accepts the obvious one: InferRequest.infer accepts an int index, a port NAME, or a ConstOutput, and REJECTS the Output port object; InferRequest.get_tensor accepts the Output port object or a ConstOutput and REJECTS an int index, while get_output_tensor(0) accepts the int. So the input for infer and the output for get_tensor cannot both be keyed the same way, and a caller that assumes they can finds out at runtime, on a booth. The port index app.inference.decode keys on is a key this project assigns, not one OpenVINO accepts for either call.

layout_cross_check.note: derived by separate code from the same observation; a match is evidence, a mismatch is a bug in one of the two

anchor_count_check.note: a post-NMS output would carry a small frame-dependent count, not the raw anchor count, so this is evidence independent of the op census that the export does not suppress

activation_ops_in_graph.note: the export carries activation ops, which is consistent with the measured value ranges of the class block (rows 4..83 all within [0,1], max 0.909073 over a real frame) and is why app.inference.decode does not apply a second one. Which op is responsible for which block is NOT claimed here - the value range is the measurement, this is only corroboration.

has_embedded_nms_evidence: walked all 734 ops (24 distinct types) and found no NonMaxSuppression of any version; the output is static [1, 84, 8400] whose trailing extent is the raw anchor count 80^2+40^2+20^2 = 8400 for a 640 input, not a post-NMS detection count. Suppression is therefore the host's job and app.inference.decode.nms does it.
